name: Aphelios
notes: Aphelios opens with Calibrum as his main weapon and Severum in his off-hand (his fixed starting loadout); Moonlight Vigil is cast at t=0 while Calibrum is main, so its weapon-specific bonus always resolves as Calibrum's empowered mark bonus.

The main weapon is modeled cycling Calibrum -> Gravitum -> Infernum -> Crescendum -> Calibrum... as its 50-Moonlight magazine is spent by attacks (1 Moonlight) and Q casts (10 Moonlight), each depletion causing a 1 s assembly (no attacks) and a 1.5 s lock on the new weapon's Q, exactly as described.

Off-hand is modeled as staying Severum for the entire fight: off-hand Moonlight is only spent by ability-triggered attacks (Calibrum's snipe, Duskwave's volley, Sentry's copy), which are comparatively rare, so the off-hand weapon is assumed never to exhaust inside this fight. A direct consequence is that Severum never becomes the main weapon, so Onslaught is never cast in this simulation -- a documented simplification, not a claim that Onslaught has no value in real play.

Because the off-hand never becomes Crescendum, Crescendum never accumulates spectral Chakrams (those are generated only by other weapons' triggered attacks while Crescendum is off-hand, or by Moonlight Vigil while Crescendum is main); Crescendum's own basic attack is therefore modeled as a plain 100% AD hit with no stacking bonus, and its throw-and-return attack lock is not modeled (assumed point-blank engagement, per one of the dossier's own proposed readings, so travel time is treated as negligible).

Binding Eclipse (Gravitum's Q) can only be cast once a Gravitum basic attack has landed and its slow is still active; it is cast the instant that becomes true and is recast whenever both its own cooldown and a fresh slow window allow it.

Duskwave's off-hand volley is modeled as crit-affected and applying on-hit effects, following the ability's headline description rather than its self-contradicting note that the automatic attacks trigger no on-attack effects at all -- the higher-damage, more commonly cited reading.

Sentry is deployed on cooldown while Crescendum is main; it is assumed to arm and immediately find the target (point-blank placement), then attacks at Aphelios' own attack speed for its 4 s active window at full crit-chance effectiveness.

Weapon Master's bonus stats are modeled on a fixed schedule that matches maxOrder: attack-damage points cap out by champion level 6, then attack-speed points cap out by level 12 (both capped at 6 points); its bonus lethality is not modeled since the engine exposes no hook to add bonus lethality to damage mitigation.

Moonlight Vigil's extra crit-damage-modifier scaling (0 to 30 percentage points across its ranks) is not applied: its formula references stat hooks the numbers sheet could not resolve, and the wiki itself documents an unexplained bug in this exact area, so ordinary crit damage is used instead.

Calibrum's mark is treated as a single consumable flag per target (never stacking) and is consumed by the very next basic attack after Moonshot lands; Moonshot is recast on cooldown whenever Calibrum is main.
Infernum's cone and secondary bolts require other enemies behind the primary target to hit anything, so against a single dummy only the primary 110% AD hit is dealt.

W and E have no combat effect in this fight (Phase is a pure weapon-order toggle we do not use since the main-weapon cycle already matches the intended order, and the Weapon Queue System is a display-only slot); their cooldownS lists are copied flat from the numbers sheet/ddragon at every rank purely to satisfy the by-rank format, and neither is ever cast by the driver.
Mana costs are not modeled: nothing here binds inside an 8-15 s fight at level 16.
